Scholarship and Internship

Amazon Future Engineer students can boost their future for themselves and their community with the support of college funding, paid internship opportunities, and industry mentors.

Up to $40,000 for your engineering or computer science degree - plus an opportunity for a paid Amazon internship!

The AFE Scholarship is so much more than a scholarship. It covers up to $10,000 per year (for 4 years) toward the cost of a degree. But the support doesn’t end there. AFE scholars get access to a network of professionals to help grow their careers — plus mentorship, mental health resources, and a chance at an opportunity to intern with Amazon.

The Amazon Future Engineer scholarship is built for what’s next, and we want you to apply. Two engineering tracks — Software Development Engineering and Automation Engineering.

You could be awarded up to $40,000 in scholarship funds, mentorship and an opportunity to intern at Amazon. Your curiosity can go a long way. You could be one of the students chosen for this opportunity — there’s only one way to find out.

Apply now!

This year, we’ve made a BIG change!

AFE is now supporting both Automation Engineering and Software Development Engineering.

Choose this track if...

Automation Engineering

You’re curious about conveyor systems, robotics, packaging, machines, and automated sortation systems that keep our facilities running efficiently.
You like hands-on work that keeps you moving and tinkering.

You like the flexibility that comes with shift work.

A typical day: you might diagnose an electrical issue in the morning and calibrate a robotic arm in the afternoon. You’ll often work independently across fulfillment centers, sortation centers, delivery stations, and air hubs.

Software Development Engineering

You’re inspired to build the code and systems that run the Amazon ecosystem: Amazon.com, Alexa, AWS, and more.

You prefer mostly desk-based work that involves meetings and collaboration.

You appreciate the consistency of standard business hours.

A typical day: you might design a new feature in the morning, review a teammate’s code around midday, and debug a production issue in the afternoon. You’ll work in small teams that own the full cycle of product development.

Eligibility requirements

Be a high school senior in the U.S. who is currently enrolled in or who has completed a high school or college dual degree course where computer science, engineering, or robotics is the subject. Students who have not taken this course can opt-in to take an assessment offered by Amazon.

Must be authorized to work in the U.S. Example: Employment Authorization Document holder, Permanent Resident, or U.S. Citizen.

Must demonstrate financial need. This opportunity is to support students with a substantial need for financial assistance.

Have a minimum cumulative grade point average of 2.3 on a 4.0 scale (or its equivalent).

Plan to attain a bachelor’s degree

Automation Engineering
■ Electrical Engineering, Automation Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering or Related Field
Software Development Engineering
■ Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Information Systems or Related field

Frequently Asked Questions

Amazon will award up to $10,000 each year of your 4-year degree program (up to $40,000 total). If you have a funding gap that is less than $10,000 each year, the AFE scholarship will completely cover it. For example, if you have a funding gap of $8,000 annually, the Amazon Future Engineer scholarship will pay out $8,000 each year for a total of $32,000. If you have a funding gap of $14,000 annually, the Amazon Future Engineer scholarship will pay out $10,000 each year for a total of $40,000.
Click the “Apply Now” button above and follow the instructions. You will need your high school transcripts, your parents'/guardians most recent 1040 tax forms, and proof that you have completed a high school or college dual degree course where computer science, engineering, or robotics is the subject. If you have not already taken this course, you can take a test to prove your skills here.
If you are selected as a finalist, you will be asked to take an assessment specific to your selected track (Software Development Engineer or Automation Engineer). Your scores will be considered alongside the rest of your application. Finalists will receive more information in late January, and you will have one week to complete the assessment.
Automation Engineering

A. You can study Electrical Engineering, Automation Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering or Related Field

Software Development Engineering

A. You can study Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Information Systems or Related field
We will first select finalists. Once the finalists are notified, they will be asked to take an assessment (this is not to be confused with the assessment to test out of the CS course mentioned above). After all finalist assessments are evaluated, we will select and notify the winners.
The two AFE tracks are Automation Engineering and Software Development Engineering. To choose the plan that’s best for you, review the program-specific FAQs below. Each track leads to a different kind of engineering and different potential careers.
No, you must select the track that best matches your degree program and career goals.
Scholars who meet eligibility requirements have a chance for a 3-month, paid internship at Amazon, based on available positions. Every internship is different because every day at Amazon is different. Depending on which track you choose (Automation Engineering or Software Development Engineering), you will either be working on the floor, maintaining and calibrating our robotics and conveyor systems, or you’ll be working in an office designing and building the code that runs all of our systems and programs. No matter which track you choose, you will get hands-on experience in your chosen field and ownership over your internship project.
Software Development Engineers (SDEs) are responsible for designing, building, and maintaining the software and systems that power everything from the Amazon.com shopping experience and Alexa to the automation running inside Amazon’s fulfillment centers, AWS, and more. They spend their days writing, reviewing, and debugging the code that runs everything.
An Automation Engineer at Amazon is responsible for designing, programming, and optimizing the automated systems that power Amazon’s fulfillment and sortation centers. This includes working with robotics, conveyor systems, and other cutting-edge technology to keep operations running efficiently.
Check out: https://scholarshipamerica.org/scholarship/amazonfutureengineer/
Please e-mail: AmazonFutureEngineer@ScholarshipAmerica.org and we’ll get back to you within two business days.
